message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study performs a meta-analysis of preclinical efficacy studies of sunitinib, calculating pooled effect sizes (SMD) and assessing their relationship with clinical outcomes. It quantifies agreement by evaluating the predictive value of preclinical studies and the potential for publication bias, which directly relates to the concordance of animal model results with human clinical outcomes.",
  "arm": "efficacy",
  "arm_evidence": "We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of features of design and outcomes for preclinical efficacy studies of the highly successful drug sunitinib.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "oncology"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "A meta-analysis of threats to valid clinical inference in preclinical research of sunitinib. Sunitinib is licensed as monotherapy for three different malignancies.",
  "model_type": "xenograft-pdx",
  "model_evidence": "Figure 1. Descriptive analysis of ( A ) internal, construct, and ( B ) external validity design elements. External validity scores were calculated for each malignancy type tested, according to the formula: number species used + number of models used; an extra point was assigned if a malignancy type tested more than one species and more than one model.",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Figure 1A shows that experiments predominantly relied on juvenile, female, immunocompromised mouse models, and very few animal efficacy experiments used genetically engineered cancer models (n = 4) or spontaneously arising tumors (n = 0).",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Our primary outcome was experimental tumor volume and we extracted necessary information (sample size, mean measure of treatment effect, and SDM/SEM) to enable calculation of study and aggregate level effect sizes."
}
